body.statement: The two monotone full laws in \(\mathfrak E_3\) constructed from \(q^-_{ihj}\) and \(q^+_{ihj}\), with \(R(0)=\infty\), the common randomized treatment mechanism, and \(C=3\), induce the same observed-data law \(P\).  Both satisfy \(D(0)\le D(1)\), but their values of \(\ell_\star\) are \(-1/20\) and \(1/4\), respectively.  Consequently \(\ell_\star\), and hence the joint pair \((\theta_\nu,\rho_\nu)\), is not point identified in any nonparametric causal model class containing both laws.  This upward nonidentification implication does not assert that \(\Theta_I(P)\) remains sharp after the maintained terminal-monotonicity class is enlarged.
body.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{prop{:}strict\text{-}cross\text{-}cohort\text{-}support}\), both arrays are probability laws supported on \(D(0)\le D(1)\), both have control within-arm margin \(\mu_0^\star\) after \(R(0)=\infty\) is attached, and both have treated within-arm margin \(\mu_1^\star\).  The construction of \(\mathfrak E_3\) uses in both cases the same degenerate distribution of \(X\), the same independent treatment law \(\Pr(Z=1)=1/2\), and the same censoring time \(C=3\).  Under consistency, conditional on \(Z=z\) the observed pair \((D,R)\) has law \(\mu_z^\star\).  Hence, for every measurable set \(A\) in the observed path space,
\[
\Pr(O\in A)
=\frac12\Pr_{\mu_0^\star}\{O(0)\in A\}
 +\frac12\Pr_{\mu_1^\star}\{O(1)\in A\},
\]
where the at-risk and event-history components of \(O(z)\) are deterministic measurable functions of \((D(z),R(z),C,z,X)\).  The right-hand side is identical for the two full laws, proving that they induce the same \(P\).

The same proposition gives their distinct attained values
\[
\ell_\star=-\frac1{20}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\ell_\star=\frac14.
\]
Thus the two full laws are observationally equivalent but disagree on a linear functional of the TV-SACE surface.  They therefore disagree on the joint surface pair as well, irrespective of the deterministic RM relation \(\rho_\nu(a,t)=-\int_0^a\theta_\nu(r,t)\,dr\).  If a larger nonparametric causal class contains both laws, the same pair remains an observational-equivalence witness inside that class, so point identification fails there.  This containment argument transfers only nonidentification upward: once terminal monotonicity or another maintained restriction is removed, it supplies neither necessity nor sufficiency of the marked-capacity fiber and therefore does not establish sharpness of \(\Theta_I(P)\) for the enlarged class.
